Read this before interpreting the table

Risk is not a benchmark. High means a plausible high-volume or expensive-capture path when the relevant event/provider is enabled. It does not prove a significant measured slowdown. Disabled-provider overhead, Debug-only instrumentation, and payload preparation are called out separately.

Snapshot & history

The cutoff is the end of 30 April 2026 UTC, using the last reachable repository commit selected before 1 May. This is source history, not a claim about a particular released Windows App SDK package.

Rename-aware comparison: the May source-mirror migration moved the old src\ tree to the root. Baseline paths are mapped before comparing event identities; a moved file is not counted as a new event.

What “all” covers

Both enabled and conditionally compiled producers are catalogued. Legacy manifest declarations without a direct emitter are retained and explicitly labelled, rather than presented as definitely logged. Start and Stop records are distinct where the producer defines separate records.

OS/kernel, GPU-driver, application, dependency-internal and test/sample providers are outside the WinUI production-event inventory. Debug output alone is not an ETW event. Compiler/tooling producers, if found, are labelled separately.

Coverage, extraction method, and limitations

Performance points worth checking first

How to interpret enabled and disabled costs
  • Enabled volume: per-element Measure/Arrange/render, property changes, input updates and item-realization events can produce many small records. A Begin/End pair doubles that record count.
  • Collection cost: formatting, URI/type-name capture, AutomationPeer creation, COM property reads, heap queries, stack capture, buffer copies and tree traversal can cost more than the ETW write.
  • No listener: an internal writer check does not automatically avoid evaluating C++ function arguments or earlier preparation. For manifest Trace* macros, the generated conditional gates expressions inside the macro; preceding statements and independent instrumentation counters remain outside that protection.
  • Debug / build gates: code excluded from retail builds adds no shipping code-path cost. Do not transfer a profiler-build overhead conclusion to retail without checking its build gate.
  • Capture setup: stackwalking, broad provider keywords, buffer configuration, trace consumers and disk pressure change observer overhead. The event’s level is not itself a cost rating.
  • Region duration is not logger duration: a long Start-to-Stop span measures the underlying operation, not the time spent emitting its two markers. Establish real overhead with comparable capture-on/capture-off measurements.
